# Details

**DESCRIPTION**

Load and plot the circular GLMM fitted in `HS_circGLMM_fit.ipynb` to describe waggle-run angles relative to the feeder for dances on horizontal and vertical combs at medium solar elevations.

**INPUTS**

`HS_functions.R`, `0Data/hs_dance_reorg.csv`, `0Data/hs_dance_medel_VH.feather`, `2Results/HS_unwrap_condition.nc`

**OUTPUTS**

Plotted estimates, predictions and contrasts.

**REFERENCES**

**modelling methods**

- Sayin S, ...
  Graving JM, $\textit{et~al}$.(2025) The behavioral mechanisms governing collective motion in swarming locusts.
  $\textit{Science}$ 387,995-1000 [DOI:10.1126/science.adq7832](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.adq7832)

- Graving JM, Sayin S, Costelloe BR, Goldshtein A & Foster JJ. Unwrapping circular statistics with Bayesian multilevel models.

- Abril-Pla, O., Andreani, V., Carroll, C., Dong, L., Fonnesbeck, C. J., Kochurov, M., Kumar, R., Lao, J., Luhmann, C. C., Martin, O. A., et al. (2023).
  `PyMC`: a modern, and comprehensive probabilistic programming framework in Python.
  *PeerJ Computer Science* 9, e1516.

- Capretto, T., Piho, C., Kumar, R., Westfall, J., Yarkoni, T., & Martin, O.
  (2022) `Bambi`: A simple interface for fitting Bayesian linear models in Python. *Journal of Statistical Software* 103(15), 1-29. <doi:10.18637/jss.v103.i15>

- Seyboldt, A., Carlson, E. L., & Carpenter, B.
  (2026).
  Preconditioning Hamiltonian Monte Carlo by minimizing Fisher Divergence.
  *arXiv* preprint arXiv:2603.18845.

# Motivation

Dances on a horizontal comb are oriented directly towards the feeder, whereas dances on a vertical comb transpose the sun's azimuth into the direction of gravity.
Here we compare the mean direction ($\mu$) and directional consistency ($\kappa$) of waggle runs relative to the feeder between these two conditions, at medium solar elevations ($30° <$ `sun_el` $< 45°$).

The model fitted was:

$\mu \sim$ V + (1 + V |Individual) + (1 |Dance)

$\kappa \sim$ V + (1 + V |Individual) + (1 |Dance)

where V is $0$ for horizontal and $1$ for vertical dances.
Each dance was performed in a single condition, so dances (nested within individuals) have random intercepts only.

# Set up workspace

To extract these models, we need to load the appropriate functions.
Make sure that the `circular`, `reticulate`, `arrow`, `posterior` and `bayesplot` packages are installed.
Here we use the `HS-env` conda environment created for `HS_circGLMM_fit.ipynb`, so that `arviz` can read the saved model.

```{r Load functions and packages}
source('HS_functions.R')
require(reticulate) #run python from R
use_condaenv("HS-env",
             required = TRUE)
reticulate::py_config()
#load .feather files (readable in R and Python)
require(arrow)
#process and plot MCMC data
require(posterior)
require(bayesplot)
options(posterior.num_args = list(sigfig = 3))#for ease of reading

#condition colours, as in HS_ExploratoryPlots.Rmd
cond_cols = list(
  vertical = 'darkred',
  horizontal = 'darkgreen'
)
```

# Prepare data

Then load the data that will be used.
This is our dance data, reorganised as `hs_dance_reorg.csv`, from which we select the same subset as in `HS_circGLMM_fit.ipynb`.

```{r Load data}
#Dance angle data
hd = read.table(file = '0Data/hs_dance_reorg.csv',
                header = T,
                sep  = ',')
#select medium elevations and the vertical or horizontal conditions
medel_min = 30 # degrees
medel_max = 45 # degrees
hd = subset(hd,
            sun_el > medel_min &
              sun_el < medel_max &
              condition %in% c('vertical', 'horizontal')
            )
head(hd)
```

## Format data

Ensure that each variable has the correct data format for subsequent analysis.

```{r Data formatting}
hd = within(hd,
            {
              ID = droplevels(as.factor(ID)) # bee identifier as a factor
              ID_d = droplevels(as.factor(ID_d)) # dance identifier as a factor
              condition = factor(condition,
                                 levels = c('horizontal', 'vertical'))
              angle = feeder_angle # angle relative to feeder, between -pi and pi
              angle_deg = deg(feeder_angle) # in degrees, for plotting
            }
)
u_id = with(hd, unique(ID)) # unique bees
length(u_id)#23 bees
u_dance = with(hd, unique(ID_d)) # unique dances
length(u_dance)#88 dances
```

To align individual and dance numbers from the model with the names in the `data.frame` we need to load these columns from the `pandas` version of the data.
This data is saved in a `.feather` file (readable in both `R` and `Python`).

```{r Load the data in pandas format}
hd_pd = read_feather(file = "0Data/hs_dance_medel_VH.feather",
                     col_select = c('Individual', 'Dance', 'Dance_label'))
#check that the same rows were selected in the same order
stopifnot(nrow(hd_pd) == nrow(hd),
          all(hd_pd$Dance_label == as.character(hd$ID_d)))
#find individuals and dances
hd = within(hd,
            {
              Individual_nr = hd_pd$Individual
              Dance_nr = hd_pd$Dance
            }
            )
#lookup tables for individuals and dances
id_tab = unique(hd[, c('ID', 'Individual_nr')])
id_tab = id_tab[order(id_tab$Individual_nr), ]
dance_tab = unique(hd[, c('ID_d', 'Dance_nr', 'ID', 'Individual_nr', 'condition')])
dance_tab = dance_tab[order(dance_tab$Dance_nr), ]
n_ind = nrow(id_tab)
n_dance = nrow(dance_tab)
```

# Load Bambi model and extract draws for each parameter

This loads draws from our fitted Bayesian model's posterior distribution.
Because the model was built and saved in `Python`, we use the `reticulate` package to interface directly with `Python` libraries from within our `R` environment.

**Parameter Structural Hierarchies**

The model parameters are categorised into two groups based on their structural hierarchy: Population-Level (Global) Parameters (`global_params`) and Group-Level (Random) Effects (`group_params`), the latter for both individuals and dances.

Converting the whole posterior to a data frame (`idata$posterior$to_dataframe()`) would cross the individual and dance dimensions (as well as each observation's predictions), so instead we extract each parameter separately as an array of `chain` $\times$ `draw` (`\times` level).

```{r Load the model}
# Define Parameter Groupings
global_params = c(
  "Intercept", "V",
  "kappa_Intercept", "kappa_V",
  "1|Individual_kappa", "V|Individual_kappa", "1|Dance_kappa",
  "kappa_1|Individual_sigma", "kappa_V|Individual_sigma", "kappa_1|Dance_sigma"
)

group_params = c(
  "1|Individual", "V|Individual", "1|Dance",
  "kappa_1|Individual", "kappa_V|Individual", "kappa_1|Dance"
)

#Import arviz for model handling
az = reticulate::import("arviz")
# Load the NetCDF file
idata = az$from_netcdf("2Results/HS_unwrap_condition.nc")
```

## Reshaping posterior draws into wide format

Each parameter array is reshaped so that draws run sequentially within each chain, and each level of a group-level effect becomes its own column, named by its level in the model (e.g. `1_Individual_5`, `kappa_1_Dance_17`).
The level names are the `Individual` and `Dance` codes from `hs_dance_medel_VH.feather`.

- **Parameter Extraction**: `py_get_item` extracts each parameter as an `xarray.DataArray`, whose values are converted to an `R` array.

- **Dynamic Pivoting**: Group-level effects have their special syntax characters replaced (\| to \_) for column safety and are pivoted out into one column per level.

- **Posterior Class Conversion**: The wide data frame is converted into a `draws_df` object using the `posterior` package.

```{r Reorganise draws by individual and dance}

# Reshape posterior draws -------------------------------------------------
post = idata$posterior
draws_list = list()
for(param in c(global_params, group_params))
{
  da = reticulate::py_get_item(post, param)
  vals = da$values # chain x draw (x level)
  if(length(dim(vals)) == 2)
  {
    # draws within chains
    draws_list[[param]] = as.vector(t(vals))
  }else
  {
    dim_name = unlist(da$dims)[3]
    lvls = as.character(reticulate::py_get_item(da$coords, dim_name)$values)
    mat = matrix(aperm(vals, c(2, 1, 3)),
                 ncol = dim(vals)[3])
    clean_base = gsub(pattern = "\\|",
                      replacement =  "_",
                      x =  param)
    for(j in seq_along(lvls))
    {
      draws_list[[paste0(clean_base, "_", lvls[j])]] = mat[, j]
    }
  }
}
n_chains = dim(reticulate::py_get_item(post, 'Intercept')$values)[1]
obs_per_chain = dim(reticulate::py_get_item(post, 'Intercept')$values)[2]
draws_wide = data.frame(.chain = rep(x = 1:n_chains, each = obs_per_chain),
                        .iteration = rep(x = 1:obs_per_chain, times = n_chains),
                        draws_list,
                        check.names = FALSE)
#check that every individual and dance was found
stopifnot(all(paste0("1_Individual_", id_tab$Individual_nr) %in% colnames(draws_wide)),
          all(paste0("1_Dance_", dance_tab$Dance_nr) %in% colnames(draws_wide)))

# Export to draws dataframe
draws_final = posterior::as_draws_df(draws_wide)
```

# Inspect model estimates

```{r Inspect main effects}
mcmc_trace(draws_final,
           pars = c('Intercept', 'V'),
           transformations = unwrap_circular_deg)
mcmc_trace(draws_final,
           pars = paste0("kappa_",
                         c('Intercept', 'V')) )
mcmc_trace(draws_final,
           pars = c('1|Individual_kappa',
                    'V|Individual_kappa',
                    '1|Dance_kappa') )
mcmc_trace(draws_final,
           pars = c('kappa_1|Individual_sigma',
                    'kappa_V|Individual_sigma',
                    'kappa_1|Dance_sigma') )
```

Check the $\hat{R}$ values for the unwrapped estimates (convergence is indicated by $\hat{R}<1.01$).

```{r summarise fixef with arviz}
azsum_fixed = az$summary(idata,
           var_names=c("Intercept",
               "V",
                "kappa_Intercept",
               "kappa_V"
                ),
    circ_var_names=c("Intercept",
                    "V"
                    )
)
print(azsum_fixed[, c(1, 3, 4, 7, 9)], digits = 3)
```

```{r summarise ranef with arviz}
azsum_ranef = az$summary(idata,
           var_names=c( "1|Individual_kappa",
        "V|Individual_kappa",
        "1|Dance_kappa",
        "kappa_1|Individual_sigma",
        "kappa_V|Individual_sigma",
        "kappa_1|Dance_sigma"
                )
)
print(azsum_ranef[, c(1, 3, 4, 7, 9)], digits = 3)
```

# Extract predictions

To look at the model estimates in context and compare the predictions with the data, we need to extract and summarise the draws.
The posterior can be summarised by its quantiles: `quantile(x, probs = c(0.025, 0.975))` identifies the interval containing the central $95\%$ of draws for `x`.

On a circular scale the bounds between which quantiles should be counted are not clearly defined, but `mod_circular` ensures data fall between $-180°$ and $180°$; since angles relative to the feeder are centred near $0°$, this boundary falls far from the bulk of the estimates.

```{r set up functions to summarise draws}

#A function to find the circular median in (-pi, pi)
MedCDraws = function(x,
                     templ = 'none', #assumes radians
                     medn = 1) #take the 1st median
{
  median.circular( circular(x = mod_circular(x),
                            template = templ)
                                           )[medn]
}
#A function to report circular quantiles in degrees
QDegDraws = function(x,
                     probs = c(0.5, 0.025, 0.975))
{
  round(deg(
    quantile(mod_circular(x), probs = probs)
  ))
}
#A function to report linear quantiles
QDraws = function(x,
                  probs = c(0.5, 0.025, 0.975),
                  digits = 2)
{
  round(quantile(x, probs = probs),
        digits = digits)
}
```

## Population-level predictions for each condition

```{r Population predictions}
pop_draws = with(draws_final,
                 list(
                   mu = list(h = Intercept,
                             v = Intercept + V),
                   kappa = list(h = kappa_Intercept,
                                v = kappa_Intercept + kappa_V)
                 )
)

pred_table = data.frame(
  condition = c('horizontal', 'vertical'),
  mu_median = sapply(pop_draws$mu, function(x){QDegDraws(x)[1]}),
  mu_lower = sapply(pop_draws$mu, function(x){QDegDraws(x)[2]}),
  mu_upper = sapply(pop_draws$mu, function(x){QDegDraws(x)[3]}),
  kappa_median = sapply(pop_draws$kappa, function(x){QDraws(softplus(x))[1]}),
  kappa_lower = sapply(pop_draws$kappa, function(x){QDraws(softplus(x))[2]}),
  kappa_upper = sapply(pop_draws$kappa, function(x){QDraws(softplus(x))[3]}),
  rho_median = sapply(pop_draws$kappa, function(x){QDraws(A1(softplus(x)), digits = 3)[1]}),
  rho_lower = sapply(pop_draws$kappa, function(x){QDraws(A1(softplus(x)), digits = 3)[2]}),
  rho_upper = sapply(pop_draws$kappa, function(x){QDraws(A1(softplus(x)), digits = 3)[3]}),
  row.names = NULL
)
print(pred_table)
```

## Extracting individual- and dance-specific predictions

This section combines population-level and group-level parameters to compute the posterior predictions for each individual in each condition, and for each dance in the condition in which it was performed.

**Processing Workflow**

- **Dynamic Variable Fetching**: A loop iterates through each individual (or dance) code, fetching that specific individual's random intercept and condition effect draws from the wide data frame.

- **Linear Combination Reconstruction**: The population-level effects are recombined with the individual-level (and dance-level) deviations to reconstruct the specific direction ($\mu$) and consistency ($\kappa$).

- **Nested Storage Architecture**: The raw vectors are assigned to a nested list (`individual_draws`) to preserve the entire distribution for downstream circular analysis.
Concurrently, point-estimate summaries (medians) are calculated and stored in separate vectors.

```{r Extract individual predictions}
# Setup containers for summary statistics
mu_id_h = kappa_id_h = numeric(n_ind)
mu_id_v = kappa_id_v = numeric(n_ind)

# Create one Master List for all raw draws
# Structure: individual_draws[[i]]$mu$h
individual_draws = vector("list", n_ind)

for(i in id_tab$Individual_nr) {

  calc = within(
    draws_final,
    {
      # Dynamic fetch
      m_i   = get(paste0("1_Individual_", i))
      m_vi  = get(paste0("V_Individual_", i))

      k_i   = get(paste0("kappa_1_Individual_", i))
      k_vi  = get(paste0("kappa_V_Individual_", i))

      # Calculate Raw Vectors
      h_mu_vec = Intercept + m_i
      h_ka_vec = kappa_Intercept + k_i

      v_mu_vec = Intercept + m_i + V + m_vi
      v_ka_vec = kappa_Intercept + k_i + kappa_V + k_vi
    }
  )

  # Save to the Nested List
  individual_draws[[i]] = list(
    mu    = list(h = calc$h_mu_vec,
                 v = calc$v_mu_vec),
    kappa = list(h = calc$h_ka_vec,
                 v = calc$v_ka_vec)
  )

  # Store summary stats for quick table access
  mu_id_h[i] = MedCDraws(calc$h_mu_vec)
  kappa_id_h[i] = median(calc$h_ka_vec)

  mu_id_v[i] = MedCDraws(calc$v_mu_vec)
  kappa_id_v[i] = median(calc$v_ka_vec)
}
```

Each dance was performed in a single condition, so its prediction combines the population, individual and dance-level effects for that condition only.

```{r Extract dance predictions}
mu_dance = kappa_dance = numeric(n_dance)

for(d in dance_tab$Dance_nr)
{
  i = dance_tab$Individual_nr[dance_tab$Dance_nr == d]
  cnd = as.character(dance_tab$condition[dance_tab$Dance_nr == d])
  cc = c(horizontal = 'h', vertical = 'v')[cnd]
  mu_d = individual_draws[[i]]$mu[[cc]] +
    draws_final[[paste0("1_Dance_", d)]]
  ka_d = individual_draws[[i]]$kappa[[cc]] +
    draws_final[[paste0("kappa_1_Dance_", d)]]
  mu_dance[d] = MedCDraws(mu_d)
  kappa_dance[d] = median(ka_d)
}
```

### Visualising individual predictions

This section loops through individual bees to plot observed waggle$~$runs against the model's posterior predictions for each condition.
The raw circular data are displayed alongside density contours derived from the joint posterior distribution of $\mu$ and $\kappa$ for that individual.
Thin arrows show the median estimated mean$~$vector for each dance, and the thick arrow shows the median estimated mean$~$vector for the individual.
Conditions in which an individual did not dance are left blank.

```{r Plot the individual predictions, fig.height = 10, fig.width = 10}

par(pty = 's')
par(mar = c(0,0,0,0),
    mfrow = c(4,4) )
for(i in id_tab$Individual_nr)
{
  indiv = as.character(id_tab$ID[id_tab$Individual_nr == i])
  for(cnd in c('horizontal', 'vertical'))
  {
    cc = c(horizontal = 'h', vertical = 'v')[cnd]
    dt_ic = subset(hd,
                   Individual_nr == i &
                     condition %in% cnd)
    if(!nrow(dt_ic))
    {
      plot.new()
      mtext(text = paste(indiv, '\nno', cnd, 'dances'),
            side = 1,
            line = -2)
      next
    }
    with(dt_ic,
    {
      PCfun(angles = angle_deg,
           col = cond_cols[[cnd]],
           plot_rho = FALSE,
           title = paste(indiv, cnd))
      }
    )
    Draws2Cont(individual_draws[[i]],
             x_string = paste0('sin(mu$', cc, ') * A1(softplus(kappa$', cc, '))'),
             y_string = paste0('cos(mu$', cc, ') * A1(softplus(kappa$', cc, '))')
    )
    #dance estimates
    for(d in unique(dt_ic$Dance_nr))
    {
      arrows.circular(
        x = circular(mu_dance[d],
                     units = 'radians',
                     rotation = 'clock',
                     zero = pi/2),
        y = A1(softplus(kappa_dance[d])),
        lwd = 0.5,
        length = 0,
        col = adjustcolor(cond_cols[[cnd]], alpha.f = 200/255)
      )
    }
    #individual estimate
    arrows.circular(
      x = circular(switch(cc, h = mu_id_h[i], v = mu_id_v[i]),
                   units = 'radians',
                   rotation = 'clock',
                   zero = pi/2),
      y = A1(softplus(switch(cc, h = kappa_id_h[i], v = kappa_id_v[i]))),
      lwd = 5,
      length = 0.1/1.25,
      col = adjustcolor(cond_cols[[cnd]], alpha.f = 0.8)
    )
  }
}

```

## Plot population level predictions

### Calculating empirical descriptors and paired shifts

This section calculates descriptive circular metrics from the raw data and identifies individuals that danced in both conditions.

**Analysis Pipeline**

- **Circular Summary Extraction**: Computes mean vector lengths (`rho.circular`), maximum likelihood parameters (`MLE_est`), and Rayleigh uniformity tests (`Rayleigh_p`) for each individual in each condition using `aggregate`.
These are saved to `mean_vectors`, alongside a linearised precision metric (`iskappa`).

- **Cohort Filtering**: Individuals in `vh_ids` danced in both conditions.

- **Empirical Delta Processing**: Calculates descriptive shifts in individual headings ($\Delta\mu$) from horizontal to vertical using `MuDiff`.

```{r Calculate estimates of means and changes}

#calculate mean vectors
mean_vectors = aggregate(angle~ID*condition,
                         data = hd,
                         FUN = function(x){rho.circular(circular(x, template = 'none'))}
)
#correct names
mean_vectors = within(mean_vectors,
                      {mean_vector = angle; rm(angle)} # angle now indicates a mean vector, not an angle
)
#add kappa
mle_estimates = aggregate(angle~ID*condition,
                          data = hd,
                          FUN = MLE_est
)
#Rayleigh tests
rayleigh_tests = aggregate(angle~ID*condition,
                          data = hd,
                          FUN = Rayleigh_p
                          )
#add to the summary table and
#calculate inverse softplus kappa
mean_vectors = within(mean_vectors,
                      {
                        mu = deg(mle_estimates$angle[,'mu'])
                        kappa = mle_estimates$angle[,'kappa']
                        iskappa  = inv_softplus(kappa)
                        rayleigh_p = rayleigh_tests$angle
                      }
)

luc = sapply(u_id,
              FUN = IndCond,
              dta = hd,
              vars = 'condition')

#Individuals that danced in both conditions
vh_ids = u_id[luc == 2]
length(vh_ids)

#condition specific
h_ids = with(subset(hd,
                    subset = condition %in% 'horizontal'),
             unique(ID)
             )
v_ids = with(subset(hd,
                    subset = condition %in% 'vertical'),
             unique(ID)
             )

mu_diff_v = sapply(X = vh_ids,
                   FUN = MuDiff,
                   dta = mean_vectors,
                   vars = 'condition',
                   val = 'vertical',
                   ref_val = 'horizontal')
```

### Visualising population-level circular predictions

This section generates side-by-side population-level visualisations for the two conditions.
It combines empirical mean dance directions, individual estimates, and population model predictions.

**Visualisation Components**

- **Empirical Baselines**: Plots individual mean directions (`mu`) from the data using `PCfun`.

- **Individual Estimates**: Thin background arrows (`arrows.circular`) showing the median estimated mean$~$vector for each individual that danced in that condition.

- **Posterior Uncertainty Contours**: Uses `Draws2Cont` to summarise the model's posterior distribution density for each condition.

- **Population Model Estimates**: Thick foreground arrow representing the population's median estimated mean$~$vector.

```{r Plot population level predictions, fig.height = 5, fig.width = 10}
par(pty = 's')
par(mfrow = c(1,2), mar = c(0,0,0,0))

# Population mean for horizontal (Baseline: Intercept)
with(subset(mean_vectors, condition %in% 'horizontal'), {
  PCfun(angles = mu, col = cond_cols$horizontal, shrink = 2, plot_rho = FALSE,
        title = 'horizontal')
})

for(i in id_tab$Individual_nr[id_tab$ID %in% h_ids]) {
  arrows.circular(x = circular(x = mu_id_h[i], units = 'radians', rotation = 'clock', zero = pi/2),
                  y = A1(softplus(kappa_id_h[i])), lwd = 0.25, length = 0,
                  col = adjustcolor(cond_cols$horizontal, alpha.f = 200/255))
}

Draws2Cont(draws = draws_final,
           x_string = 'sin(Intercept) * A1(softplus(kappa_Intercept))',
           y_string = 'cos(Intercept) * A1(softplus(kappa_Intercept))')

with(draws_final,
     arrows.circular(x = circular(x = MedCDraws(Intercept),
                                  units = 'radians',
                                  rotation = 'clock', zero = pi/2),
                     y = A1(median(softplus(kappa_Intercept))),
                     lwd = 5, length = 0.1/1.25,
                     col = adjustcolor(cond_cols$horizontal, alpha.f = 200/255, offset = c(rep(-0.2,3),0) )
     )
)

# Population mean for vertical (Intercept + V)
with(subset(mean_vectors, condition %in% 'vertical'), {
  PCfun(angles = mu, col = cond_cols$vertical, shrink = 2, plot_rho = FALSE,
        title = 'vertical')
})

for(i in id_tab$Individual_nr[id_tab$ID %in% v_ids]) {
  arrows.circular(x = circular(x = mu_id_v[i], units = 'radians', rotation = 'clock', zero = pi/2),
                  y = A1(softplus(kappa_id_v[i])), lwd = 0.25, length = 0,
                  col = adjustcolor(cond_cols$vertical, alpha.f = 200/255))
}

Draws2Cont(draws = draws_final,
           x_string = 'sin(Intercept + V) * A1(softplus(kappa_Intercept + kappa_V))',
           y_string = 'cos(Intercept + V) * A1(softplus(kappa_Intercept + kappa_V))')

with(draws_final,
     arrows.circular(x = circular(x = MedCDraws(Intercept + V), units = 'radians', rotation = 'clock', zero = pi/2),
                     y = A1(median(softplus(kappa_Intercept + kappa_V))),
                     lwd = 5, length = 0.1/1.25, col = adjustcolor(cond_cols$vertical, alpha.f = 200/255, offset = c(rep(-0.2,3),0)))
)

print("Horizontal mean direction")
with(draws_final, QDegDraws(Intercept))
print("Vertical mean direction")
with(draws_final, QDegDraws(Intercept + V))
```

### Plotting the relative population-level effect

This section visualises the difference in direction between conditions and prints summary quantiles for the directional shift.

**Visualisation Components**

- **Empirical Differences**: Plots the observed differences in mean dance angle (vertical $-$ horizontal) for individuals that danced in both conditions, using `PCfun`.

- **Individual Vectors**: median estimates of the change in direction for each of those individuals.

- **Posterior Densities**: Projects posterior distribution contours for the effect of condition ($V$), scaled by the concentration of that effect across individuals (`V|Individual_kappa`), using `Draws2Cont`.
N.B. `V|Individual_kappa` is a von Mises concentration estimated directly (LogNormal prior), so it is not transformed by `softplus`.

- **Population Shift**: Overlays a thick arrow representing the estimated median population-level shift.

- **Turn Size Quantiles**: Computes and prints the median and $95\%$ credible intervals for the directional shift and for individual turning magnitudes.

```{r Plot relative pop level effects, fig.height = 5, fig.width = 5}
par(pty = 's')
par(mfrow = c(1,1), mar = c(0,0,0,0))

# --- Effect of vertical comb ---
PCfun(angles = unlist(mu_diff_v),
      col = 'gray40',
      shrink = 2,
      plot_rho = FALSE,
      title = 'vertical - horizontal')

for(i in id_tab$Individual_nr[id_tab$ID %in% vh_ids]) {
  arrows.circular(x = circular(x = mu_id_v[i] - mu_id_h[i],
                               units = 'radians',
                               rotation = 'clock',
                               zero = pi/2),
                  y = A1(softplus(kappa_id_v[i])),
                  lwd = 0.5,
                  length = 0,
                  col = adjustcolor('gray60', alpha.f = 200/255))
}
#scale by alignment _across_ individuals
Draws2Cont(draws = draws_final,
           x_string = 'sin(V) * A1(`V|Individual_kappa`)',
           y_string = 'cos(V) * A1(`V|Individual_kappa`)')

with(draws_final,
     arrows.circular(x = circular(x = MedCDraws(V),
                                  units = 'radians',
                                  rotation = 'clock',
                                  zero = pi/2),
     y = A1(median(`V|Individual_kappa`)),
     lwd = 5,
     length = 0.1/1.25,
     col = adjustcolor('gray40', alpha.f = 200/255, offset = c(rep(-0.2,3),0))
     )
)
print("Effect of vertical comb on direction")
with(draws_final, QDegDraws(V))

#individual turns: for individuals that danced in both conditions
vh_nr = id_tab$Individual_nr[id_tab$ID %in% vh_ids]
turn_mat = sapply(vh_nr,
                  function(i)
                  {
                    abs(mod_circular(individual_draws[[i]]$mu$v -
                                       individual_draws[[i]]$mu$h))
                  }
                  )
print("Effect of vertical comb on mean individual turn size")
QDraws(deg(rowMeans(turn_mat)), digits = 0)
```

### Visualising consistency predictions

This section visualises the posterior distributions for concentration parameters ($\kappa$) and prints summary quantiles for concentration and estimated mean vector lengths (`A1(kappa)`).

**Visualisation & Summary Components**

- **Consistency ($\kappa$)**: Plots a $1 \times 2$ grid of vertical histograms (`VertHist`) showing the posterior density of estimated concentration parameters for each condition.

- **Quantile Reporting**: Computes median estimates and $95\%$ credible intervals for each condition.

```{r Kappa predictions}
#plot kappa
par(mfrow = c(1,2))
kappa_lim = with(draws_final,
                 range(softplus(c(kappa_Intercept, kappa_Intercept + kappa_V))))

with(draws_final,
     VertHist(data = softplus(kappa_Intercept),
              main = '\nhorizontal',
              ylab = 'kappa',
              ylim = kappa_lim,
              col = adjustcolor(cond_cols$horizontal, alpha.f = 100/255),
              cex.axis = 0.7))

with(draws_final,
     VertHist(data = softplus(kappa_Intercept + kappa_V),
              main = '\nvertical',
              ylab = 'kappa',
              ylim = kappa_lim,
              col = adjustcolor(cond_cols$vertical, alpha.f = 100/255),
              cex.axis = 0.7))

print("Horizontal kappa")
with(draws_final, QDraws(softplus(kappa_Intercept)))
print("Vertical kappa")
with(draws_final, QDraws(softplus(kappa_Intercept + kappa_V)))
```

### Changes in consistency

- **Contrast Effects ($\Delta\kappa$)**: Plots the change in concentration from horizontal to vertical, with a dashed baseline marker (`abline`) at no change.

```{r Kappa effects}
# Plot difference in kappa
par(mfrow = c(1,2))

# Effect of vertical comb (vertical - horizontal)
with(draws_final,
     VertHist(data = softplus(kappa_Intercept + kappa_V) - softplus(kappa_Intercept),
              main = '\nDiff: kappa',
              ylab = 'diff kappa',
              col = adjustcolor('gray40', alpha.f = 100/255),
              cex.axis = 0.7))
abline(h = 0, lty = 2)

with(draws_final,
     VertHist(data = A1(softplus(kappa_Intercept + kappa_V)) - A1(softplus(kappa_Intercept)),
              main = '\nDiff: mean vector',
              ylab = 'diff mean vector length',
              col = adjustcolor('gray40', alpha.f = 100/255),
              cex.axis = 0.7))
abline(h = 0, lty = 2)

#Report effects
#effect on kappa
print("effect of vertical comb on kappa")
with(draws_final,
     QDraws(softplus(kappa_Intercept + kappa_V) -
              softplus(kappa_Intercept))
)
#effect on mean vector
print("effect of vertical comb on mean vector length")
with(draws_final,
     QDraws(A1(softplus(kappa_Intercept + kappa_V)) -
              A1(softplus(kappa_Intercept)),
            digits = 3)
)
#probability of a decrease in consistency
print("probability that vertical dances are less consistent")
with(draws_final,
     round(mean(kappa_V < 0), digits = 3)
)
```

### Visualising the concentration across individuals and dances

To interpret how similarly individuals and dances were oriented, we extract the posterior distributions for the group-level concentrations ($\kappa_\mu$).
These were estimated directly as von Mises concentrations (LogNormal priors), so no transformation is needed.

**Analysis Workflow**

- **Scale Transformation**: Since some effects may be extremely consistent ($\kappa_{\mu} \to \infty$), they are plotted on a $\log_{10}$ scale.

- **Custom Axis Mapping**: To maintain intuitive interpretation, custom logarithmic axis ticks (`lticks`) are overlaid with the original linear values as text labels.

- **Contrast Profiles**: "Horizontal" (`1|Individual_kappa`) is the concentration of individual mean directions around the population mean for horizontal dances, the "vertical effect" (`V|Individual_kappa`) is the concentration of individual changes in direction from horizontal to vertical, and "dances" (`1|Dance_kappa`) is the concentration of dance mean directions around their individual's mean direction.

```{r Kappamu effects}
#plot kappa
par(mfrow = c(1,3))

lticks = c(1,3,5, 1:10*10, 200, 300)

#"Horizontal" (Intercept)
with(draws_final,
     VertHist(data = log10(`1|Individual_kappa`),
              main = '\nhorizontal',
              ylab = 'kappamu',
              ylim = log10(c(1, 300)),
              col = adjustcolor(cond_cols$horizontal, alpha.f = 100/255),
              axes = FALSE,
              cex.axis = 0.7))
axis(1)
axis(2, at = log10(lticks), labels = lticks)

#Vertical effect
with(draws_final,
     VertHist(data = log10(`V|Individual_kappa`),
              main = '\nvertical effect',
              ylab = 'kappamu',
              ylim = log10(c(1, 300)),
              col = adjustcolor(cond_cols$vertical, alpha.f = 100/255),
              axes = FALSE,
              cex.axis = 0.7))
axis(1)
axis(2, at = log10(lticks), labels = lticks)

#Dances within individuals
with(draws_final,
     VertHist(data = log10(`1|Dance_kappa`),
              main = '\ndances',
              ylab = 'kappamu',
              ylim = log10(c(1, 300)),
              col = adjustcolor('gray50', alpha.f = 100/255),
              axes = FALSE,
              cex.axis = 0.7))
axis(1)
axis(2, at = log10(lticks), labels = lticks)

print("Concentration of individuals (horizontal)")
with(draws_final, QDraws(`1|Individual_kappa`))
print("Concentration of individual vertical effects")
with(draws_final, QDraws(`V|Individual_kappa`))
print("Concentration of dances within individuals")
with(draws_final, QDraws(`1|Dance_kappa`))
```

### Estimate the posterior distribution of concentration across individuals

To evaluate the consistency of individual directional preferences within each condition, we estimate the population's concentration parameter, $\kappa_{\mu}$, using a von$~$Mises distribution.
This converts our nested list of individual MCMC draws into $Draw \times Individual$ matrices for each condition: horizontal (`h`) and vertical (`v`).
Only individuals that danced in each condition are included.

**Analysis Workflow**

- **Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE)**: The model only explicitly estimated across-individual concentration for the horizontal condition and for the *condition difference*, so across-individual concentration *within* the vertical condition needs to be estimated from the model's posterior draws.
For each MCMC draw (row), we compute the Maximum Likelihood Estimate for $\kappa$ using `mle.vonmises`.

- **Posterior Profiling**: By applying this MLE estimation across every draw, we reconstruct the full posterior distribution for $\kappa_{\mu}$ under each condition.

```{r Kappamu conditions}

# ==========================================
# MATRIX RECONSTRUCTION & HELPER FUNCTIONS
# ==========================================

# Helper function to extract a specific condition across selected individuals
# Builds a Draw-by-Individual matrix
get_mu_matrix = function(
  cond,
  inds
) {
  # sapply combines the resulting vectors into columns of a single matrix
  sapply(inds, function(i) individual_draws[[i]]$mu[[cond]])
}

# Extract matrices for each condition, for individuals observed in that condition
mu_mat_h = get_mu_matrix("h", id_tab$Individual_nr[id_tab$ID %in% h_ids]) # Horizontal
mu_mat_v = get_mu_matrix("v", id_tab$Individual_nr[id_tab$ID %in% v_ids]) # Vertical


# ==========================================
# MAXIMUM LIKELIHOOD ESTIMATION (MLE)
# ==========================================

# Function to calculate the MLE kappa (concentration parameter) for a single draw row
calc_kappa_mle = function(
  mu_row
) {
  # mle.vonmises returns a complex list object; we extract only the numeric $kappa estimate
  as.numeric(mle.vonmises(circular(mu_row, units='radians'))$kappa)
}

# Apply the MLE function across all rows (MARGIN = 1) of each matrix
post_kappamu_h = apply(mu_mat_h, 1, calc_kappa_mle)
post_kappamu_v = apply(mu_mat_v, 1, calc_kappa_mle)


# ==========================================
# VISUALIZATION (VERTICAL HISTOGRAMS)
# ==========================================
par(mfrow = c(1,3))
kappamu_lim = range(c(post_kappamu_h, post_kappamu_v))

VertHist(data = post_kappamu_h,
         main = '\nhorizontal', ylab = 'kappamu (MLE)',
         ylim = kappamu_lim, col = adjustcolor(cond_cols$horizontal, alpha.f = 100/255),
         cex.axis = 0.7)

VertHist(data = post_kappamu_v,
         main = '\nvertical', ylab = 'kappamu (MLE)',
         ylim = kappamu_lim, col = adjustcolor(cond_cols$vertical, alpha.f = 100/255),
         cex.axis = 0.7)

diff_kappamu = post_kappamu_v - post_kappamu_h
VertHist(data = diff_kappamu,
         main = '\nDiff: vertical', ylab = 'diff kappamu',
         col = adjustcolor('gray40', alpha.f = 100/255),
         cex.axis = 0.7)
abline(h = 0, lty = 2)

print("Effect of vertical comb on concentration across individuals")
QDraws(diff_kappamu, digits = 3)
print("Effect of vertical comb on mean vector length across individuals")
QDraws(A1(post_kappamu_v) - A1(post_kappamu_h), digits = 3)
```
